plan: This auction structure (pay second-highest bid, sealed exit prices) is equivalent to a second-price auction. In second-price auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Overbidding risks winning at a loss; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $21, I will bid exactly $21 to ensure optimal outcomes in both winning and losing scenarios.

This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the prize is worth if I win against a bid between my value and my bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, my optimal bid equals my true value of $22.

Since this is effectively a second-price sealed-bid auction (the winner pays the second-highest bid), bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Bidding higher risks winning at a price above my value (negative profit), while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $13 to maximize expected profit.
